Kamag-anak ba ng saging ang abaka?

Oo! Parehong nasa pamilyang Musa ang abaka at saging — pero itinatanim ang abaka para sa hibla, hindi para sa prutas.

Paryente ba sa saging ang abaka?

Oo! Parehas sila sa pamilyang Musa ang abaka ug saging — apan ang abaka gitanom para sa hilo, dili sa prutas.

copy.tl:

Ang gumagalaw na hangin mula sa abaniko mo ay nagpapabilis ng pagsingaw ng pawis sa balat, kaya nakakaramdam ka ng lamig!

Nganong mobati ka og kabugnaw kon ipaypay nimo ang abaniko?

Ang naglihok nga hangin gikan sa imong abaniko nagpaspas sa pag-alisngaw sa singot sa imong panit, busa mobati ka og kabugnaw!

How many active volcanoes does PHIVOLCS list in the Philippines?

PHIVOLCS lists about two dozen active volcanoes! This means they have erupted recently or still show signs of unrest today.
copy.tl:

May halos dalawampu't apat na aktibong bulkan sa listahan ng PHIVOLCS! Ibig sabihin, nagputok sila kamakailan o may palatandaan pa ng galaw.
copy.bis:
Pila ka aktibo nga bulkan ang naa sa listahan sa PHIVOLCS sa Pilipinas?

Naa'y mga kapin sa baynte-upat ka aktibo nga bulkan sa listahan sa PHIVOLCS! Pasabot, nagputok sila bag-o o nagpakita pa og kalihukan.

Unsa ang kinabababaan nga posibleng temperatura?

Ang absolute zero ang kinabababaan nga posibleng temperatura, ug kini kay -273.15 degrees Celsius, o -273.15°C!

Why is an acid sour?

When an acid dissolves in water, it releases hydrogen ions (H+)! The amount of H+ decides exactly how acidic it is.
copy.tl:
Bakit maasim ang isang acid?

Kapag natunaw sa tubig, naglalabas ito ng hydrogen ions (H+)! Ang dami ng H+ ang nagpapasiya kung gaano ito ka-acid.
copy.bis:
Nganong maaslom ang acid?

Kung matunaw sa tubig, nagpagawas kini og hydrogen ions (H+)! Ang gidaghanon sa H+ ang nagtino kung unsa kini ka-acid.

copy.tl: Ang activated carbon ay puno ng maliliit na pores na kumukuha ng unwanted chemicals sa pamamagitan ng adsorption! Kaya ginagamit ito sa water filters para tanggalin ang masamang lasa at amoy.
copy.bis: Ang activated carbon puno sa gagmay nga pores nga nagbitad sa unwanted chemicals pinaagi sa adsorption! Mao nga gigamit kini sa water filters aron tangtangon ang daotang lasa ug baho.

copy.tl: Ang fault na gumalaw kamakailan at maaaring gumalaw muli ay tinatawag na aktibong fault! Kaya binabantayan ito ng PHIVOLCS para sa posibleng lindol.
copy.bis: Ang fault nga bag-o lang nilihok ug lagmit molihok pag-usab gitawag og aktibo nga fault! Mao nga gibantayan kini sa PHIVOLCS para sa posibleng linog.

copy.en: The adrenal glands sit right above your kidneys — when you're scared or excited, they release adrenaline that speeds up your heartbeat.
copy.tl: Ang adrenal glands ay nasa ibabaw ng bato — kapag takot o nasasabik ka, naglalabas ito ng adrenaline na nagpapabilis ng tibok ng puso.
copy.bis: Ang adrenal glands anaa sa ibabaw sa imong bato — kon mahadlok o maukyab ka, mopagawas kini og adrenaline nga nagpadali sa pitik sa kasingkasing.

copy.en:
Why does your stomach feel uneasy when you're nervous?

When adrenaline kicks in, it slows down digestion because energy is sent to the muscles and heart first. That's why your stomach can feel uneasy or you lose your appetite when nervous.
copy.tl:
Bakit parang kumikirot ang tiyan kapag kinakabahan?

Kapag pumasok ang adrenaline, pinapabagal nito ang panunaw dahil unang ipinapadala ang lakas sa kalamnan at puso. Kaya minsan parang kumikirot ang tiyan o nawawalan ka ng gana kapag kinakabahan.
copy.bis:
Ngano morag mokumot ang tiyan kon nakulbaan?

Kon mosulod ang adrenaline, mohinay kini sa panghilis kay ang kusog ipadala una sa kaunoran ug kasingkasing. Mao nga usahay morag mokumot ang tiyan o mawad-an ka og gana kon nakulbaan ka.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion

copy.en:
Why do you shake when you're really scared?

When you're very scared, adrenaline fills your muscles with so much ready energy that they want to move even before you use it — making you shake.
copy.tl:
Bakit nanginginig ka kapag sobrang takot?

Kapag takot na takot ka, binibigyan ng adrenaline ang iyong kalamnan ng sobrang lakas na handang kumilos — kaya nanginginig ka kahit hindi mo pa ito ginagamit.
copy.bis:
Ngano mangurog ka kon grabe ka nga kahadlok?

Kon grabe ka nga kahadlok, gihatagan sa adrenaline ang imong kaunoran og sobrang kusog nga andam molihok — mao nga mangurog ka bisan wala pa nimo gamita.

What's the biggest land animal alive today?

The African elephant holds the title of the largest land animal living on Earth today!

copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga hayop sa yuta karon?

What's the biggest land animal?

The African elephant is the largest land animal! A big male can weigh almost 6 metric tons and stand more than 3 meters tall at the shoulder.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking hayop sa lupa?

Ang African elephant ang pinakamalaking hayop sa lupa! Kayang tumimbang ang malaking lalaki nito ng halos 6 toneladang metriko at tumaas nang mahigit 3 metro sa balikat.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga hayop sa yuta?

Ang African elephant mao ang pinakadako nga hayop sa yuta! Ang dako nga laki niini makatimbang og halos 6 ka metriko nga tonelada ug makataas og kapin 3 ka metro sa abaga.

Why do valleys give rain and river warnings after a big eruption?

Because lahars can come at night, days later! Even when the crater is quiet, listen to these warnings to stay safe.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbibigay ng babala sa ulan at ilog ang mga lambak pagkatapos ng malaking pagsabog?

Dahil pwedeng dumating ang lahars sa gabi, ilang araw pagkatapos! Kahit tahimik na ang bulkan, makinig sa mga babala.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang mga walog naghatag og pahimangno sa ulan ug sapa human sa dakong pagsabog?

Kay ang lahar pwede moabot sa gabii, pila ka adlaw human! Bisan kalma na ang bulkan, pamati ang mga pahimangno.

copy.en:
What was the first Philippine satellite launched into orbit?

Agila-2 was the first! Launched in 1997, it was a Philippine satellite used for communications.
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang satelayt ng Pilipinas na inilunsad sa orbit?

Ang Agila-2 ang una! Inilunsad ito noong 1997 bilang satelayt ng Pilipinas na ginamit sa komunikasyon.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang unang satelayt sa Pilipinas nga gilusad ngadto sa orbita?

Ang Agila-2 ang una! Gilusad kini niadtong 1997 isip satelayt sa Pilipinas nga gigamit sa komunikasyon.

copy.en: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is just a tiny piece of the air we breathe — only about 0.04%! But plants really need it to grow.
copy.tl: Ang carbon dioxide (CO2) ay napakaliit na bahagi lang ng hangin — halos 0.04%! Pero kailangan ito ng mga halaman para lumaki.
copy.bis: Ang carbon dioxide (CO2) gamay ra kaayong bahin sa hangin — mga 0.04%! Pero kinahanglan kini sa mga tanom aron motubo.

copy.tl: Ang aircon ay nagpapalipas ng hangin sa malalamig na coils na sumisipsip ng init at halumigmig, kaya lumalamig ito!
copy.bis: Ang aircon nagpaagi sa hangin sa bugnaw nga coils nga nagsuyop sa init ug halumigmig, mao nga mobugnaw ang hangin!

copy.en: The atmosphere, the layer of air around Earth, contains elements like oxygen and nitrogen as gases, and helium as a very light gas.
copy.tl: Ang atmosphere, ang layer ng hangin sa paligid ng Earth, ay naglalaman ng mga element tulad ng oxygen at nitrogen bilang gas, at helium bilang napakagaan na gas.
copy.bis: Ang atmosphere, ang layer sa hangin sa palibot sa Earth, adunay mga element sama sa oxygen ug nitrogen isip gas, ug helium isip gaan kaayo nga gas.

copy.en: Every time you breathe in, air rushes into your body through your nose and mouth!
copy.tl: Tuwing huminga ka, dumadaloy ang hangin papasok sa katawan mo sa pamamagitan ng iyong ilong at bibig!
copy.bis: Matag ginhawa nimo, mosulod ang hangin sa imong lawas agi sa imong ilong ug baba!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trapped air is a good insulator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions trapped air as an insulator but does not explain the particle model or the processes underlying conduction or convection. copy.en:
Why do thick sweaters and fluffy fur keep us warm?

Trapped air is a good insulator! Tiny air pockets in them keep the heat in.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagpapanatili ng init ang makapal na swetersa at balahibo ng hayop?

Ang nakulong na hangin ay mahusay na insulator! Ang maliliit na bulsa ng hangin sa mga ito ay nagpapanatili ng init.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagpabilin sa init ang baga nga sweater ug balhibo sa hayop?

Ang nabilanggo nga hangin maayo nga insulator! Ang gagmay nga lungag sa hangin niini magpabilin sa init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air is full of gas particles

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gas particles in air but does not describe the Particle Model of Matter as a general model (all matter made of tiny particles, each pure substance having its own kind). It only gives a single example without explaining the model.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a vacuum has no sound, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations. The sound reference is a consequence of vacuum, not an exploration of sound production or transfer.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card says air is full of gas particles but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It does not name any component gases.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air is full of gas particles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gas particles but does not identify the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or classify air as a gas. It does not teach the states of matter.

copy.en:
What is the difference between air and a vacuum?

Air is full of gas particles, but a vacuum has no air at all! Outer space is nearly a vacuum, so there is no sound there.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinagkaiba ng air at ng vacuum?

Ang air ay puno ng gas particles, pero ang vacuum ay walang hangin! Halos vacuum ang outer space, kaya walang tunog doon.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kalainan sa air ug sa vacuum?

Ang air puno sa gas particles, apan ang vacuum walay hangin! Halos vacuum ang outer space, busa walay tingog didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air thinner with less oxygen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It focuses on altitude effects, not the composition of air.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathlessness but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. No pictures or diagrams are involved.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air and oxygen but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It is about altitude effects, not the general concept of basic needs.

copy.en: Climbing high mountains like Mount Apo makes the air thinner with less oxygen. That’s why climbers feel out of breath and tire easily!
copy.tl: Ang pag-akyat sa matataas na bundok gaya ng Mount Apo ay nagpapamanipis ng hangin at nagpapakaunti ng oxygen. Kaya nahihirapan huminga at madaling mapagod ang mga climbers!
copy.bis: Ang pagsaka sa taas nga bukid sama sa Mount Apo nagpapamanipis sa hangin ug nagpapagamay sa oxygen. Mao nga ang mga climbers maglisod og ginhawa ug daling makapoy!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Breathing dirty air harms our lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs but does not identify respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) from pictures/diagrams or describe how they work. It only states that dirty air harms lungs, which is not direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Breathing dirty air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air but does not identify air as a basic need of living things. It focuses on harm from dirty air, not on the basic needs themselves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Breathing dirty air harms our lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Breathing dirty air harms our lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies that dirty air is harmful, but it does not recognize the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. No conservation or protection message is present.

copy.en: Breathing dirty air harms our lungs and can cause coughing, asthma, and other illnesses.
copy.tl: Ang paghinga ng maruming hangin ay nakakasama sa ating baga at maaaring magdulot ng ubo, hika, at iba pang sakit.
copy.bis: Ang pagginhawa sa hugaw nga hangin makadaot sa atong baga ug mahimong hinungdan sa ubo, hubak, ug uban pang sakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The outside air pressure is lower up high

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure, which is one of the weather characteristics listed in the competency, but it does not teach identification of weather characteristics. assignedReviews.card_evidence: letting the air inside push the rubber outward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves gas behavior (air inside a balloon) but does not describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. It does not state that gases have no definite shape or volume, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does a balloon get bigger as it rises?

The outside air pressure is lower up high, letting the air inside push the rubber outward!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumalaki ang isang lobo kapag pinataas?

Mababa ang presyon ng hangin sa labas sa itaas, kaya itinutulak ng hangin sa loob ang goma palabas!
copy.bis:
Nganong modako ang globo samtang mosaka kini?

Ubos ang presyon sa hangin sa gawas sa ibabaw, mao nga itukmod sa hangin sa sulod ang goma pagawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The steam condenses

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes condensation, a change of state, but the competency requires describing changes of state using diagrams and flowcharts. assignedReviews.card_evidence: The steam condenses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a temperature change causing condensation (gas to liquid), which is a change of state, but the competency focuses on solid to liquid to gas (melting, evaporation) and does not include condensation. The card does not directly support the specific state changes listed in the competency.

copy.en: Plunge a hot tin can with steam into cold water, and it crumples! The steam condenses, and the stronger outside air pressure crushes the can.
copy.tl: Ilubog ang mainit na lata na may steam sa malamig na tubig, at ito ay babagtok! Nag-co-condense ang steam, at ang malakas na outside air pressure ang pumipisil sa lata.
copy.bis: Ilubog ang mainit nga lata nga adunay steam sa bugnaw nga tubig, ug madurog kini! Nag-condense ang steam, ug ang mas kusog nga outside air pressure ang nagdurog sa lata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the strong outside air pressure squishes it flat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure, which is one weather characteristic, but it does not teach identifying weather characteristics or describe weather. It is a physics demonstration of air pressure crushing a can, not a lesson on weather descriptors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When steam inside a can cools down fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves condensation (steam cooling to liquid), a change of state, but it does not describe changes of state using diagrams or flowcharts, nor does it systematically teach melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation. It only illustrates one effect of rapid cooling and pressure difference.

copy.en: Crush a can! When steam inside a can cools down fast, the strong outside air pressure squishes it flat!
copy.tl: Durog ang lata! Kapag biglang lumamig ang singaw sa loob, dinudurog ito ng malakas na presyon ng hangin sa labas!
copy.bis: Dugmok ang lata! Kung kalit nga mabugnaw ang aso sa sulod, dugmukon kini sa kusog nga presyon sa hangin sa gawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air pressure decreases because there is simply less air above you
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure, which is one of the weather characteristics listed in the competency, but it explains the altitude dependence of air pressure rather than identifying air pressure as a basic weather descriptor. It does not directly support the skill of identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en: As you go higher up, air pressure decreases because there is simply less air above you!
copy.tl: Habang umaakyat ka sa mas mataas na lugar, bumababa ang air pressure dahil mas kaunti ang hanging nasa itaas mo!
copy.bis: Samtang mosaka ka sa mas habog nga dapit, mokunhod ang air pressure tungod kay gamay ra ang hangin sa ibabaw nimo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air pressure changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure, which is one of the weather characteristics listed in the competency, but the card is about ear popping during airplane ascent/descent, not about identifying weather characteristics. It does not teach that air pressure is a descriptor of weather or how it is used in weather observation.

copy.en: When a plane climbs or drops, air pressure changes! Your body equalises the pressure on both sides of your eardrum, causing that fun 'pop' in your ears.
copy.tl: Kapag umaahon o bumababa ang eroplano, nagbabago ang air pressure! Inaayos ng katawan mo ang presyon sa magkabilang panig ng eardrum, kaya naririnig mo ang 'pop' sa tainga.
copy.bis: Pag mo-angat o mo-lusong ang eroplano, mag-usab ang air pressure! Gi-ayo sa imong lawas ang presyon sa duha ka bahin sa eardrum, mao na ang 'pop' sa imong tainga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat the air inside a bottle, then cool it! The air shrinks, pressure drops, and stronger outside air pushes the egg right in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a temperature-pressure phenomenon but does not mention particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or that they move faster with heat. It does not directly teach the particle model competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat the air inside a bottle, then cool it! The air shrinks, pressure drops, and stronger outside air pushes the egg right in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves temperature change affecting air, but it does not describe changes in properties of materials like wood or coal burning. It is about air pressure, not material property changes due to temperature.

copy.en: Heat the air inside a bottle, then cool it! The air shrinks, pressure drops, and stronger outside air pushes the egg right in!
copy.tl: Painitin ang hangin sa bote, tapos palamigin! Lumiliit ang hangin, bumababa ang pressure, at itinutulak ng mas malakas na hangin sa labas ang itlog papasok!
copy.bis: Init-a ang hangin sulod sa botelya, unya pabugnawa! Mogamay ang hangin, mokunhod ang pressure, ug ang mas kusog nga hangin sa gawas motulod sa itlog sulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One pascal equals one newton of force on each square meter.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the pascal as a unit of pressure using newtons, but it does not teach that forces act between objects or how forces are measured. It only mentions a force unit incidentally, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We measure it in pascals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card introduces the pascal as a pressure unit, but the competency focuses on identifying and using units in simple science activities such as milligrams, grams, kilograms, and degrees centigrade. Pascal is not among the listed units and the card does not address appropriate use in simple activities, so it is only related by being a unit.

copy.en:
How do we measure pressure?

We measure it in pascals! One pascal equals one newton of force on each square meter.
copy.tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang presyon?

Sinusukat natin ito sa pascal! Ang isang pascal ay katumbas ng isang newton na puwersa sa bawat metro kuwadrado.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsukod sa presyon?

Gisukod nato kini sa pascal! Ang usa ka pascal katumbas sa usa ka newton nga kusog sa matag metro kuwadrado.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the average air pressure is about 101 kilopascals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific value of air pressure at sea level but does not identify air pressure as a characteristic used to describe weather, nor does it connect the value to weather conditions. It shares the vocabulary 'air pressure' but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 101 kilopascals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the unit kilopascals, but the competency focuses on identifying and appropriately using units in simple science activities, with examples like mg, g, kg, and °C. Kilopascals is not among the listed units, and the card does not teach unit identification or usage in a science activity context.

copy.en:
How heavy is the air pushing down on us at sea level?

At sea level, the average air pressure is about 101 kilopascals, which is also called 1 atmosphere!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang hangin na tumutulak sa atin sa antas ng dagat?

Sa antas ng dagat, ang karaniwang air pressure ay mga 101 kilopascals, o katumbas ng 1 atmosphere!
copy.bis:
Pila ka kabug-at ang hangin nga moduso kanato sa lebel sa dagat?

Sa lebel sa dagat, ang kasagarang air pressure mga 101 kilopascals, o katumbas sa 1 atmosphere!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you pull the plunger, you lower the pressure inside. Then, outside air pressure pushes the liquid right in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how air pressure moves liquid in a syringe, but G3-F-1 focuses on making objects move by natural causes (wind, water) or by people (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying). Air pressure is not one of the listed causes, and the card does not explore or demonstrate the general ways objects move; it only explains a specific pressure phenomenon. This is same broad subject (forces/motion) but not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how a syringe sucks up liquid?

When you pull the plunger, you lower the pressure inside. Then, outside air pressure pushes the liquid right in!
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung paano sumisipsip ang hiringgilya ng likido?

Kapag hinila mo ang plunger, bumababa ang presyon sa loob. Kaya itinutulak ng presyon ng hangin sa labas ang likido papasok!
copy.bis:
Natinga ka ba kung giunsa pagsuyop sa jeringa og likido?

Kung birahon nimo ang plunger, mokunhod ang presyon sa sulod. Mao nga itukmod sa presyon sa hangin sa gawas ang likido pasulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has very low air pressure! This pulls air inward and makes the winds spin faster.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure and wind, but it does not teach identification of basic weather characteristics in general; it presents a specific fact about typhoon center pressure and wind spin, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has very low air pressure! This pulls air inward and makes the winds spin faster.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about low pressure at a typhoon's center, but it does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, and it does not involve gathering information from secondary sources.

copy.en:
What happens at the center of a typhoon?

It has very low air pressure! This pulls air inward and makes the winds spin faster.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa gitna ng isang bagyo?

May napakababang presyon ng hangin! Humihigop ito ng hangin papasok at lumalakas ang mga hangin paikot.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa sentro sa usa ka bagyo?

Adunay ubos kaayo nga presyon sa hangin! Mosuyop kini og hangin pasulod ug mopakusog sa paglibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That push is the air you're shoving away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes air resistance as a push felt when moving fast, but the competency requires planning and carrying out an investigation on how different surfaces affect frictional forces. The card does not address surfaces, investigation, or friction measurement; it only touches on a force (air resistance) that is a type of fluid friction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That push is the air you're shoving away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates that air exerts a force (a push) on a moving object, which is a simple example of a force acting between objects. However, the competency also requires identifying that forces can be measured, and the card gives no information about measurement or the general concept of forces acting between objects beyond this single anecdote.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air is invisible, but you feel it when moving fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks students to identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid, or gas. The card mentions air (a gas) but does not classify it as a gas or discuss states of matter; it focuses on the force of air resistance. No direct support for classifying objects by state.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air is invisible, but you feel it when moving fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The competency defines matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The card does not mention mass, space, or the definition of matter; it only describes feeling air as a push. It does not support the concept of matter having mass and volume.

copy.en: Air is invisible, but you feel it when moving fast, like a hand out a car window! That push is the air you're shoving away.
copy.tl: Kahit hindi nakikita ang hangin, nararamdaman mo ito kapag mabilis kang gumalaw, gaya ng paglalabas ng kamay sa bintana ng sasakyan! Ang tumutulak ay ang hangin na tinatanggal mo.
copy.bis: Bisan dili makita ang hangin, mabati nimo kini kung paspas ka molihok, sama sa pagpagawas sa kamot sa bintana sa sakyanan! Kanang pagtulod mao ang hangin nga imong gitulod palayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: moisture in the air condenses on its cold coils
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions condensation as the cause of dripping water, but the competency requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card does not describe the change of state process, nor does it use diagrams or flowcharts, and it does not cover the other required state changes.

copy.en:
Why does an air conditioner drip water?

It drips water because moisture in the air condenses on its cold coils!
copy.tl:
Bakit tumutulo ng tubig ang aircon?

Tumutulo ito ng tubig dahil ang singaw sa hangin ay namumuo sa malamig nitong tubo!
copy.bis:
Nganong motulo og tubig ang aircon?

Motulo kini og tubig kay ang alisngaw sa hangin mamuok sa bugnaw niini nga tubo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it removes heat from inside the room!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat but does not address the difference between heat and temperature, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it removes heat from inside the room!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to heat but does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it connect heat energy to causing change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it removes heat from inside the room!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat removal but does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes such as melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it removes heat from inside the room!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any changes of state or use diagrams/flowcharts; it only states that an air conditioner removes heat.

copy.en: Like a fridge, an air conditioner does not make cold; it removes heat from inside the room!
copy.tl: Tulad ng ref, ang aircon ay hindi gumagawa ng lamig kundi inaalis ang init sa loob ng kwarto!
copy.bis: Sama sa ref, ang aircon dili maghimog bugnaw kondili magkuha sa kainit sulod sa kwarto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After eruptions, airlines reroute because even a modest Philippine blast can send ash high enough to hurt airplane engines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why airlines reroute around volcanic ash clouds, which is a consequence of eruptions. It does not discuss patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years, nor does it assess or describe how predictable eruption patterns are. The content is only tangentially related to volcanic activity and does not directly support the competency's focus on historical patterns and predictability.

copy.en:
Why do airlines reroute around ash clouds?

After eruptions, airlines reroute because even a modest Philippine blast can send ash high enough to hurt airplane engines!
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-rereroute ang mga airline sa paligid ng ash clouds?

Pagkatapos ng pagputok, nag-rereroute ang mga airline dahil kahit modest Philippine blast ay maaaring itulak ang ash pataas na makakasira sa makina!
copy.bis:
Nganong mo-reroute ang mga airline palibot sa ash clouds?

Human sa pagputok, mo-reroute ang mga airline kay bisan modest Philippine blast makapahuyop sa ash pataas nga makadaut sa makina!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pilot turns and climbs an airplane by moving small parts on the wings and tail! These flaps and rudder change how the air flows around it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about turning and climbing an airplane using flaps and rudder, but it does not mention pushes, pulls, speed, or stopping. It only relates to changing direction in a general sense, without directly supporting the competency's focus on demonstrating pushes and pulls.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These flaps and rudder change how the air flows around it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that moving small parts changes airflow and affects movement, but it does not describe the listed factors (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture) that affect movement. The connection to the competency is only topical.

copy.en: A pilot turns and climbs an airplane by moving small parts on the wings and tail! These flaps and rudder change how the air flows around it.
copy.tl: Pinipihit at iniaangat ng piloto ang eroplano sa pamamagitan ng pagkilos ng maliliit na bahagi sa pakpak at buntot! Nagbabago ang mga flaps at rudder na ito kung paano umaagos ang hangin.
copy.bis: Pihiton ug ipataas sa piloto ang eroplano pinaagi sa paglihok sa gagmay nga bahin sa pako ug ikog! Mausab sa mga flaps ug rudder kung unsaon pag-agos sa hangin libot niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Wright brothers' very first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered a short 36 meters (120 feet)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a distance and a time for a historical event, but it does not state or explain that distance divided by time is speed, nor does it ask the student to identify speed. It only supplies the two quantities, which is background information rather than direct instruction for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Wright brothers' very first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered a short 36 meters (120 feet)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions distance and time but does not involve measuring with simple equipment or any measurement activity. It is a historical fact, not a guided measurement task, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The Wright brothers' very first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered a short 36 meters (120 feet)!
copy.tl: Ang unang lipad ng magkapatid na Wright ay tumagal lamang ng 12 segundo at umabot ng 36 metro (120 talampakan) lang!
copy.bis: Ang unang lupad sa managsoong Wright milungtad lang og 12 segundo ug milakaw og 36 metros (120 ka tiil) lang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The rubbing alcohol you use to disinfect your hands is a homogeneous mixture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses homogeneous mixtures (alcohol and water), which is a chemistry/matter topic. It provides no information about animal body parts or their roles in movement and food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The rubbing alcohol you use to disinfect your hands is a homogeneous mixture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a homogeneous mixture, not about classifying Philippine animals and plants by habitat. It also does not use a drawing or diagram as required by the competency.

copy.en: The rubbing alcohol you use to disinfect your hands is a homogeneous mixture because it is a combination of water and alcohol that looks the same throughout.
copy.tl: Ang alcohol na ginagamit mong pang-disinfect ng kamay ay homogeneous mixture dahil kombinasyon ito ng tubig at alcohol na pare-pareho ang itsura sa kabuuan.
copy.bis: Ang alcohol nga imong gigamit sa pag-disinfect sa kamot usa ka homogeneous mixture tungod kay kombinasyon kini sa tubig ug alcohol nga pare-pareho ang dagway sa tibuok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS alert levels rise and fall as unrest changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how PHIVOLCS alert levels change with volcanic unrest and how communities use them to decide when to prepare or return home. It does not discuss patterns of volcanic eruptions over the last 100 years, nor does it assess or describe how predictable eruption patterns are. The content is related to volcanic monitoring and safety but does not directly support the competency's focus on historical eruption patterns and predictability.

copy.en:
How do communities know when to prepare or go home?

PHIVOLCS alert levels rise and fall as unrest changes! Communities use this pattern to decide when to get ready or go back home.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga komunidad kung kailan maghanda o umuwi?

Tumataas at bumababa ang antas ng babala ng PHIVOLCS kapag nagbabago ang kalagayan! Ginagamit ito para maghanda o umuwi.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsayod sa mga komunidad kung kanus-a mag-andam o mopauli?

Mosaka ug moubos ang lebel sa alerto sa PHIVOLCS kung mag-usab ang kahimtang! Gigamit kini sa mga komunidad aron mag-andam o mopauli.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Agar comes from red algae, and scientists use it in petri dishes as a jelly-like base to grow bacteria for study.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not teach that bacteria are unicellular or contrast them with multicellular organisms. It only uses bacteria as an example of what is grown on agar, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Agar comes from red algae, and scientists use it in petri dishes as a jelly-like base to grow bacteria for study.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions red algae and bacteria, which are living things, but it does not classify living things into the named groups using a table or similar characteristics. It provides no classification information, so it is only related by vocabulary.

copy.en: Agar comes from red algae, and scientists use it in petri dishes as a jelly-like base to grow bacteria for study.
copy.tl: Ang agar ay galing sa pulang algae, at ginagamit ito ng mga siyentipiko sa mga petri dish bilang matibay na medium para palakihin ang bacteria para pag-aralan.
copy.bis: Ang agar gikan sa pula nga algae, ug gigamit kini sa mga syentista sa mga petri dish isip solid nga medium aron padakuon ang bakterya para tun-an.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Algae make oxygen through photosynthesis too, just like phytoplankton do
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: Naming oxygen from photosynthesis is not describing the process and its raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Algae make oxygen through photosynthesis too, just like phytoplankton do
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Algae making oxygen is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Algae make oxygen through photosynthesis too, just like phytoplankton do
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using flow charts and labeled diagrams explain the role of plants and animals in the cycles of nature, such as the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use flow charts or labeled diagrams of the carbon, oxygen, or water cycles.

copy.en: Algae make oxygen through photosynthesis too, just like phytoplankton do.
copy.tl: Gumagawa rin ng oxygen ang algae sa pamamagitan ng photosynthesis, tulad ng ginagawa ng phytoplankton.
copy.bis: Naghimo usab og oxygen ang algae pinaagi sa photosynthesis, sama sa gibuhat sa phytoplankton.
